page.title: Kestrel Porch Cam — overnight on battery

blocks.heading: Kestrel Porch Cam: one night on battery, and a late package push
text: Source: Kestrel Porch Cam HLD (reviewed design, Kestrel Home platform team), the approved Backstage catalog snapshot, the reviewed code locations, and the operator's answers. Engineering view: every service hop, API operation and code reference.

Times 10:30 PM, 1:10 AM, 4:00 AM, 6:50 AM and 8:05 AM come from the operator. The other minutes (7:00 AM charging heartbeat, 8:03 AM Wi-Fi drop, 8:07 AM clip opened, 8:13 AM retry, 8:15 AM reconnect, 8:16 AM push) are illustrative, as are the 2.5 %/h net solar charge rate and the report values between drawn heartbeats.

The operator's 4:00 AM low-battery heartbeat and the HLD's ~1 %/h idle drain plus ~1 % per clip disagree: at that rate 25% at 10:30 PM would reach 20% near 2:30 AM. The camera battery is therefore held at 25% until the 4:00 AM report of 20%, and the 1 %/h rate applies only after that.

steps.text: Thu 10:30 PM. The resident goes to bed. The Porch Cam's scheduled heartbeat (battery 25%, charging no, firmware) goes over Wi-Fi through the home router to event-ingest (`POST /heartbeats`), which writes it to device-shadow. The device page now reads **Battery 25%**, last report 10:30 PM.

codeRefs.label: heartbeat route
codeRefs.purpose: Accepts a heartbeat and writes battery/charging to device-shadow

steps.text: Fri 1:10 AM. A raccoon crosses the porch. PIR wakes the camera; it records a ~20 s clip and uploads it: `POST /events` to event-ingest, then `PUT /clips/{clipId}` to clip-store. The battery is held at 25% here, because the operator's 4:00 AM low-battery time and the HLD's drain rate disagree (see the section note). The device page shows the scheduled 1:00 AM heartbeat.

steps.text: 1:10 AM. event-ingest asks motion-classifier for a label: **animal**. Animal events are saved to the timeline with no push (default user setting). event-ingest forwards only person and package events to notify-service, so nothing reaches the phone.

steps.text: 4:00 AM. The heartbeat reports **20%**. event-ingest writes it to device-shadow, whose low-battery rule marks the camera `low_battery` (at or below 20%). The device page now shows 20% with the low-battery icon.

steps.text: 4:00 AM. The low-battery rule triggers one push: notify-service sends **Porch Cam battery low** through Apple/Google push. It will not be sent again until the battery goes above 30%.

steps.text: 6:50 AM. Sunrise: the solar panel starts charging the battery. Nothing reports this yet. device-shadow and the device page still hold the scheduled 6:30 AM heartbeat, **not charging**, so the app lags the real battery until the next heartbeat.

7:00 AM. The next heartbeat reports **charging=yes** (battery 18%). event-ingest writes it to device-shadow, and the device page shows the solar charging icon. `low_battery` stays set: it re-arms only above 30%.

steps.text: 8:05 AM. A courier drops a package. PIR wakes the camera; it records a ~20 s clip (about 1% of battery) and uploads it: `POST /events` to event-ingest, then `PUT /clips/{clipId}` to clip-store. The device page holds the scheduled 8:00 AM heartbeat (20%).

steps.text: 8:07 AM. The resident opens the package clip in the Kestrel app. The HLD does not describe how the app fetches the clip, so no hop is drawn.

8:05 AM. Home Wi-Fi has been down since 8:03 AM (illustrative), after the 8:00 heartbeat got through. A courier drops a package. The camera records the ~20 s clip (about 1% of battery) to its SD card, but it cannot reach the router, so nothing reaches event-ingest or clip-store.

8:13 AM. The camera retries every 2 minutes (8:07, 8:09, 8:11, 8:13); each attempt fails at the router. The device page ages (last report still **8:00 AM**, 13 min old) but stays Online: no heartbeat has been missed yet (next due 8:30), and device-shadow marks offline only after two missed heartbeats (60 min).

shadow.note: No heartbeat missed yet (next due 8:30 AM); offline needs 2 missed (60 min).

steps.text: 8:15 AM. Wi-Fi returns, about 10 minutes after the delivery. The camera uploads the queued clip (`POST /events` to event-ingest, `PUT /clips/{clipId}` to clip-store, which accepts late uploads from SD card queues) and sends a heartbeat that event-ingest writes to device-shadow.
